# Version 4.156.0
> **Skia m156 preview** · [NuGet (prerelease)](https://www.nuget.org/packages/SkiaSharp/4.156.0-preview.1.26512.10)

> **API changes** · [SkiaSharp API diff](4.156.0/index.md) · [HarfBuzzSharp API diff](harfbuzzsharp/14.4.0.100/index.md)

## Highlights

SkiaSharp 4.156.0 previews the Skia m156 renderer with expanded native platform support. This preview restores Linux system-font discovery for NoDependencies deployments, adds native GTK4 GPU rendering, and refreshes build support for .NET 11, Windows, and Tizen.

## Breaking Changes

*None in this preview line.*

## Engine

- **Skia updated to milestone m156** — Aligns the bundled renderer with Chrome milestone 156 for consumers evaluating the next SkiaSharp release line. ([#5247](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5247))
- **Current Skia integration cleanup** — Incorporates the m155 core-fork cleanup into the current release line to keep the bundled native engine integration current. ([#5208](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5208))

## Bug Fixes

- **Linux NoDependencies font discovery restored** — NoDependencies deployments on Linux can again discover system fonts, restoring text rendering behavior that depended on the system font manager. — ❤️ [@ramezgerges](https://github.com/ramezgerges) ([#5086](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5086))

## Platform

- **Native GTK4 GPU rendering added** — GTK4 applications gain native GPU rendering with pixel-scaling support for sharper, better-aligned output. ([#5249](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5249))
- **.NET 11 native assets aligned** — Updates preview SDK pins and WebAssembly native assets so package consumers can evaluate the 4.156 line with .NET 11 previews. ([#5306](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5306))
- **Tizen native builds refreshed** — Packages and builds now target the Tizen 10 GCC 14.2 toolchain. ([#5235](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5235))

## HarfBuzzSharp 14.4.0.100

Refreshes HarfBuzzSharp native build support for .NET 11 previews, current Windows toolchains, and Tizen 10 packaging.
